name: Benchmarking Local Robustness of High-Accuracy Binary Neural Networks for Enhanced Traffic Sign Recognition
description: Traffic signs play a critical role in road safety and traffic management for autonomous driving systems. Accurate traffic sign classification is essential but challenging due to real-world complexities like adversarial examples and occlusions. To address these issues, binary neural networks offer promise in constructing classifiers suitable for resource-constrained devices. In our previous work, we proposed high-accuracy BNN models for traffic sign recognition, focusing on compact size for limited computation and energy resources. To evaluate their local robustness, this paper introduces a set of benchmark problems featuring layers that challenge state-of-the-art verification tools. These layers include binarized convolutions, max pooling, batch normalization, fully connected. reputation: A niche benchmark used in the neural network verification community to stress-test tools on challenging binary traffic-sign models.
notes: Non-LLM benchmark focused on formal verification rather than predictive accuracy; likely small and highly specialized, with difficulty driven by large parameter counts and high-dimensional inputs.
